original.target_description: Svenson (1981), single experiment: driving-safety percentile judgments relative to fellow experimental participants; US safety group and Swedish safety group both appear in Table 1. The supplied locator does not identify one of these samples. No inferential test or standardized effect size is printed.

n.quote: Forty-one of them judged their skill in driving and 40 judged how safe they were as drivers.
n.sample_role: Participants giving safety judgments; 40 US participants or 35 Swedish participants; target sample unspecified.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for these safety groups.

replication.target_description: Koppel et al. (2023), single replication study, driving-safety ratings on the 7-item Likert scale versus midpoint 4, one-sample t-test. This is the safety test on p. 4 with printed Hedges’s g, also in Table 5.

n.location: p. 5, Table 3, Panel C, Safety row
n.sample_role: Participants with safety responses in the Likert-scale condition, analytic sample for the one-sample t-test.
n.exclusions: Participants (n = 84) without a driver’s license were filtered out (p. 3). No additional exclusions for this condition are documented; 1,203 is the overall sample across response scales, not this analytic n.

es.location: p. 6, Table 5, Safety row; also p. 4, Results
es.test_statistic: t(386) = 27.38 (Table 5); p. 4 text instead prints t(386) = 27.28.

p.location: p. 6, Table 5, Safety row; also p. 4, Results

reported_success.quote: The findings from our replication are consistent with the original findings.

notes: Both retrieved full texts have titles matching the supplied references. Original locator p. 3 is Table 1 on printed p. 145; it contains separate US and Swedish safety samples and does not identify a unique sample/test. Original analytic n is therefore left null rather than choosing a country or combining groups. Original paper reports descriptive safety percentages but no inferential p, test statistic, or standardized effect size. Replication selection is the safety Likert midpoint comparison, identified by p. 4 and the requested printed Hedges’s g; Table 5 confirms it. Table 5 and p. 4 disagree on the safety t statistic (27.38 versus 27.28), while g, p bound and df agree. The two assigned inputs have the same neutral outcome and no distinguishing sample identifiers; no different test is inferred from audit ID order.
